Authors: Harrington, Saxena, Murphy, Borovykh, Yun, Kamath, Kyi, Darrell, Malik, and Bai
Title: When Does Continual Learning Require Learning
Method: Sequential LLM training and evaluation across filing years; compares prompt, fine-tuning, RL, and context-compression approaches
Outcome / Task: Direction of issuer 30-day forward stock return after the 10-K filing
Key Finding: Some update methods retain forward accuracy better than others; prompt-based approaches can overfit transient textual heuristics.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Directly studies temporal drift in a 10-K predictive task. It does not study the GenAI-era cutoff, one-year operating outcomes, calibration, controlled rewrites, or evidence-grounded defenses.
Planned Use: Highest-priority competitor; explicitly distinguish our target, period, model families, calibration analysis, and rewrite experiment.

Title: Generative AI in Financial Reporting
Document / Data: Corporate disclosures including risk factors, MD&A, earnings materials, and other reporting settings
Method: AI-writing detection validation and empirical disclosure analysis
Outcome / Task: Prevalence and characteristics of possible GenAI-assisted financial reporting
Key Finding: Documents the emergence and characteristics of possible GenAI-assisted disclosure writing.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Establishes that AI-assisted financial reporting and disclosure-language change are already active research areas.
Planned Use: Primary motivation and boundary: we do not claim to be first to study GenAI in reporting or to possess definitive authorship labels.

Title: Quantifying Semantic Shift in Financial NLP: Robust Metrics for Market Prediction Stability
Document / Data: Financial news across pre-COVID, COVID, post-COVID, and rate-hike regimes
Method: LSTM and Transformer prediction with semantic-volatility, perturbation, causal-attribution, and logical-consistency diagnostics
Outcome / Task: Next-day market prediction stability across regimes
Key Finding: Semantic volatility and distribution divergence are associated with prediction error; model robustness varies across regimes.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Directly addresses financial-NLP semantic drift, but not SEC filings, GenAI-era disclosure change, operating outcomes, or paired rewrites.
Planned Use: Use as the closest semantic-drift framework and compare its metrics with our filing-specific drift measures.

Authors: Perlin, Foguesatto, Karagrigoriou Galanos, and Affonso
Title: The Use of AI in 10-K Filings: An Empirical Analysis of S&P 500 Reports
Method: AI-content detector plus FinBERT sentiment analysis
Key Finding: Reports section-level patterns in AI-likeness and an association between detector scores and sentiment.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Very close on 10-K AI-era language measurement, but not on out-of-time predictive decay or robust alternatives.
Planned Use: Benchmark detector-based measures while emphasizing their proxy status and limited sample universe.

Title: Investor Reactions to Generative AI Usage in MD&A Disclosures
Method: Investor experiment using GenAI-created or modified MD&A
Key Finding: Tests how disclosure authorship or modification by GenAI affects investor processing and reactions.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Close on AI-modified MD&A but focuses on investor reactions rather than predictive-model reliability.
Planned Use: Supports rewrite-treatment design and disclosure-authorship framing.

Title: More Than Human: The Capital-Market Effects of AI-Generated Corporate Disclosure
Outcome / Task: Market response, spreads, analyst forecast errors, and information quality
Key Finding: Reports increasing AI-written content and associations with disclosure characteristics and capital-market outcomes.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Establishes broad capital-market consequences of AI-assisted disclosure, but not 10-K model decay or paired rewrite robustness.
Planned Use: Position our project around reliability rather than adoption or average market effects.

Title: Corporate Earnings Calls and Analyst Beliefs
Method: LLM-generated counterfactual transcripts that vary narrative emphasis while holding quantitative content fixed
Key Finding: Narrative emphasis affects predictions and analyst belief formation even when quantitative content is held fixed.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: A close methodological precedent for controlled fact-preserving text transformations.
Novelty Threat: High for rewrite novelty; Low for full project
Planned Use: Cite as the nearest counterfactual-narrative design and differentiate our paired filing robustness test.

Title: Bloated Disclosures: Can ChatGPT Help Investors Process Information?
Outcome / Task: Information content, sentiment, market reaction, and disclosure bloat
Key Finding: LLM summaries can compress disclosure text while retaining or amplifying economically relevant content.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Shows LLM transformations can alter textual measures and investor-relevant information.
Planned Use: Motivate strict factual-preservation and information-retention tests for controlled rewrites.

Title: Predict the Future from the Past? On the Temporal Data Distribution Shift in Financial Sentiment Classifications
Key Finding: Financial sentiment models can deteriorate when evaluated on later time periods.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Direct precedent for temporal degradation in financial NLP, but not SEC filings or future operating outcomes.

Title: Annual Report Readability, Current Earnings, and Earnings Persistence
Key Finding: Annual-report readability is associated with firm performance and earnings persistence.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Foundational style-dependent baseline that may be vulnerable to writing-style change.
Planned Use: Traditional readability baseline and literature replication target.

Title: When Is a Liability Not a Liability? Textual Analysis, Dictionaries, and 10-Ks
Method: Finance-specific word lists and textual measures
Key Finding: General-purpose sentiment dictionaries can misclassify financial language; domain-specific dictionaries perform better.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Canonical tone baseline whose temporal stability is central to our test.

Title: The Information Content of Forward-Looking Statements in Corporate Filings—A Naïve Bayesian Machine Learning Approach
Method: Naïve Bayes classification of forward-looking statements
Key Finding: Machine-learned forward-looking disclosure content contains information about future firm outcomes.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Foundational evidence that filing text can predict future operating outcomes.

Title: Measuring Readability in Financial Disclosures
Key Finding: Common readability formulas may be poorly suited to financial disclosures; document size can be a useful proxy.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Core baseline and warning against uncritical readability measures.

Authors: Campbell, Chen, Dhaliwal, Lu, and Steele
Title: The Information Content of Mandatory Risk Factor Disclosures in Corporate Filings
Key Finding: Mandatory risk-factor text contains economically relevant information.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports including Item 1A and testing whether its predictive content changes over time.

Title: Using 10-K Text to Gauge Financial Constraints
Outlet / Status: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
Key Finding: Constraining language in 10-Ks provides information about firms’ financial constraints.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Canonical dictionary feature for traditional-model comparisons.

Title: The Use of Word Lists in Textual Analysis
Method: Methodological review of dictionary-based text analysis
Key Finding: Word-list choice and domain fit materially affect textual-analysis results.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Guides dictionary versioning and validation under language change.

Title: Textual Analysis in Accounting and Finance: A Survey
Key Finding: Synthesizes the core methodological choices and pitfalls in financial textual analysis.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Foundational literature-map source.
Planned Use: Backward citation chaining and baseline justification.

Title: A Plain English Measure of Financial Reporting Readability
Key Finding: Develops a domain-tailored readability measure with stronger construct validity than generic formulas.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Important style baseline and alternative readability definition.

Title: Text-Based Network Industries and Endogenous Product Differentiation
Key Finding: Filing text can construct dynamic peer groups and product-market similarity.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports industry-peer similarity and convergence components.
Planned Use: Peer-language baseline and dynamic industry controls.

Title: Deep Learning Models for Bankruptcy Prediction Using Textual Disclosures
Document / Data: Corporate textual disclosures and accounting data
Key Finding: Textual disclosures can improve bankruptcy prediction beyond structured financial variables.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Strong precedent for future-adverse-outcome prediction from disclosure text.
Planned Use: Predictive baseline literature and outcome-design comparison.

Authors: Loukas, Fergadiotis, Chalkidis, Spyropoulou, Malakasiotis, and Androutsopoulos
Title: EDGAR-CORPUS: Billions of Tokens Make the World Go Round
Outlet / Status: Economics and Natural Language Processing workshop
Key Finding: Provides large-scale preprocessing conventions and evidence on the size and complexity of SEC text.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Engineering and corpus-design precedent.

Title: FinBERT: Financial Sentiment Analysis with Pre-trained Language Models
Key Finding: Domain-adapted language modeling improves financial sentiment classification.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Canonical embedding/sentiment baseline, with pretraining-cutoff issues to document.
Planned Use: Financial-domain model baseline and contamination discussion.

Title: FinQA: A Dataset of Numerical Reasoning over Financial Data
Document / Data: Financial reports with text, tables, questions, and reasoning programs
Key Finding: Financial reasoning requires linking narrative and tabular evidence through explicit computations.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports the design of evidence-linked textual and numeric features.

Title: TAT-QA: A Question Answering Benchmark on a Hybrid of Tabular and Textual Content in Finance
Document / Data: Financial reports with tables and narrative text
Method: Hybrid numerical and textual reasoning benchmark
Key Finding: Accurate financial reasoning often requires combining tabular facts with surrounding narrative evidence.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports multimodal evidence-grounded feature construction.
Planned Use: Architecture and validation precedent for claim-to-fact links.

Title: Can You Trust Your Model’s Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
Document / Data: Multiple benchmark datasets with synthetic and natural shifts
Key Finding: Uncertainty quality and calibration often deteriorate under dataset shift.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Core methodological precedent for treating calibration decay as a primary reliability outcome.

Title: Wild-Time: A Benchmark of In-the-Wild Distribution Shift over Time
Key Finding: Real-world temporal shift creates failures not captured by random train-test splits.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: General temporal-split and benchmarking precedent.

Title: Revisiting the Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
Key Finding: Architecture, pretraining, and shift conditions materially affect calibration.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports reporting calibration slope, intercept, and error rather than accuracy alone.

Title: Can AI-Generated Text Be Reliably Detected?
Document / Data: Human and machine-generated text across generators and attacks
Key Finding: Detection can be unreliable and vulnerable to distribution shift and text modification.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Directly supports treating AI-likeness as a noisy proxy rather than ground truth.

Title: GPT Detectors Are Biased Against Non-Native English Writers
Key Finding: AI detectors can produce systematic false positives and inequitable errors.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Reinforces that detector output cannot be interpreted as verified AI authorship.

Title: DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection Using Probability Curvature
Key Finding: Introduces a prominent detector approach while illustrating model- and distribution-dependence.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Potential sensitivity benchmark, not a source of definitive labels.
Planned Use: Optional detector comparison and limitation analysis.

Authors: Brown, Stephen V.; Tucker, Jennifer Wu
Title: Large-Sample Evidence on Firms’ Year-over-Year MD&A Modifications
Method: Year-over-year textual modification scores and capital-market tests
Outcome / Task: Economic change, filing reactions, and disclosure usefulness
Key Finding: MD&A modification captures economically meaningful disclosure change, while the usefulness of modification measures can vary over time.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Foundational precedent for longitudinal disclosure-change and similarity features.
Planned Use: Required year-over-year similarity baseline and interpretation guide.

Authors: Feldman, Ronen; Govindaraj, Suresh; Livnat, Joshua; Segal, Benjamin
Title: Management’s Tone Change, Post Earnings Announcement Drift and Accruals
Method: Tone-change measures combined with financial controls
Outcome / Task: Post-announcement returns and incremental disclosure information
Key Finding: Changes in management tone contain information beyond contemporaneous financial measures.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Canonical tone-change baseline that could become unstable when drafting style changes.

Title: Textual Risk Disclosures and Investors’ Risk Perceptions
Outcome / Task: Trading, volatility, and investor risk perception
Key Finding: Changes in risk disclosure are associated with changes in investor risk perceptions.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Foundational Item 1A change measure and risk-language benchmark.
Verification: Primary bibliographic and journal metadata reviewed

Title: Simultaneously Discovering and Quantifying Risk Types from Textual Risk Disclosures
Method: Topic modeling for discovery and quantification of risk types
Key Finding: Distinct textual risk categories can be discovered and linked differently to perceived risk.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Precedent for interpretable risk-topic components rather than one aggregate tone score.
Planned Use: Risk taxonomy and component-level feature audit.

Authors: Hope, Ole-Kristian; Hu, Danqi; Lu, Hai
Title: The Benefits of Specific Risk-Factor Disclosures
Key Finding: More specific risk-factor disclosures are more informative than generic risk language.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports firm-specific term density and claim-specificity components.

Authors: Dyer, Travis; Lang, Mark; Stice-Lawrence, Lorien
Title: The Evolution of 10-K Textual Disclosure: Evidence from Latent Dirichlet Allocation
Method: Topic modeling and longitudinal disclosure analysis
Outcome / Task: Long-run evolution in filing topics and properties
Key Finding: 10-K disclosure content and structure evolve materially over long horizons.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Critical warning that post-2022 differences must be separated from ordinary long-run evolution.
Planned Use: Pretrend modeling, placebo cutoffs, and historical context.

Authors: Cohen, Lauren; Malloy, Christopher J.; Nguyen, Quoc H.
Title: Lazy Prices
Document / Data: Corporate filing text and year-over-year disclosure changes
Method: Textual change measures and asset-pricing tests
Key Finding: Changes in corporate filings contain predictive information that markets may process slowly.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Major precedent for predictive power in disclosure changes.
Planned Use: Similarity/change benchmark while distinguishing operating outcomes from returns.

Authors: Kogan, Shimon; Levin, Dimitry; Routledge, Bryan R.; Sagi, Jacob S.; Smith, Noah A.
Title: Predicting Risk from Financial Reports with Regression
Key Finding: Textual representations of financial reports can predict quantitative risk outcomes.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Early direct precedent for supervised prediction from filing text.
Planned Use: Historical modeling baseline and literature chain.

Authors: Sedinkina, Marina; Breitkopf, Nikolas; Schütze, Hinrich
Title: Automatic Domain Adaptation Outperforms Manual Domain Adaptation for Predicting Financial Outcomes
Key Finding: Context-driven automatic adaptation can outperform manually adapted financial dictionaries.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Shows that fixed dictionaries may age and that context-sensitive adaptation matters.

Title: On the Risk Prediction and Analysis of Soft Information in Finance Reports
Document / Data: Narrative soft information in financial reports
Key Finding: Soft textual information can improve risk prediction and reveal interpretable risk language.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Direct soft-information prediction precedent.

Authors: Bochkay, Khrystyna; Brown, Stephen V.; Leone, Andrew J.; Tucker, Jennifer Wu
Title: Textual Analysis in Accounting: What’s Next?
Outcome / Task: Construct validity, methods, and future directions
Key Finding: Emphasizes stronger construct validation, richer textual structure, and careful alignment between measures and economic questions.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Directly informs methodological discipline and prohibited shortcut rules.

Authors: Bogachek, Olga; De Vito, Antonio; Demeré, Paul; Grossetti, Francesco
Title: Using Narrative Disclosures to Predict Tax Outcomes
Outcome / Task: Cash effective tax rates and related tax outcomes
Key Finding: Narrative topics add predictive information about future tax outcomes beyond quantitative information.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Strong evidence that 10-K narratives already predict future fundamental outcomes.
Planned Use: Prohibit broad novelty claims about predicting fundamentals from narrative disclosure.

Authors: Kim, Alex G.; Muhn, Maximilian; Nikolaev, Valeri V.; Zhang, Yijing
Title: Learning Fundamentals from Text
Method: Machine learning designed to extract information about firm fundamentals
Outcome / Task: Fundamental economic variables and future firm information
Key Finding: Text models can learn economically meaningful firm fundamentals from narrative disclosure.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Close neighbor for evidence extraction and fundamental prediction.
Planned Use: Compare our evidence-grounded definition and temporal reliability focus.
Verification: Primary SSRN and institutional pages reviewed

Authors: Gupta, Aparna; Rawte, Vipula; Zaki, Mohammed J.
Title: Predicting Firm Financial Performance from SEC Filing Changes Using Automatically Generated Dictionary
Document / Data: 10-K and 8-K filing changes, with a U.S. bank application
Method: Automatically generated dictionaries and predictive modeling
Key Finding: Automatically learned filing-change dictionaries can improve firm-performance prediction relative to standard dictionaries.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Direct overlap with disclosure changes, automatically learned language, and future financial performance.
Planned Use: Highest-priority comparison for outcome and adaptive-dictionary design.
Verification: Primary article metadata and author-hosted paper reviewed

Title: Constructing Financing and Operating Risk Measures from 10-K Text
Method: Risk-factor classification aggregated into financing and operating risk indices
Key Finding: Text-derived financing and operating risk indices behave consistently with economically related risk measures.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Directly occupies the operating-risk-from-10-K-text space.
Planned Use: Explicitly distinguish our future operating-margin outcome and reliability-under-shift question.

Authors: Zhang, Zhen; Zheng, Moxuan; Zhang, Tongchen; Lin, Luyun; Wang, Yiqing; Lin, Lixing
Title: Bankruptcy Prediction from 10-K Narratives: Evidence from Interpretable Text Scores and Accounting Baselines
Document / Data: 10-K narratives, SEC financial data, and bankruptcy events
Method: Interpretable distress dictionary plus accounting baseline with holdout and out-of-time validation
Outcome / Task: Bankruptcy during the year following the filing
Key Finding: An interpretable narrative stress score adds substantial incremental predictive value over accounting variables.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Very close on one-year future adverse outcomes, interpretable text, accounting baselines, and out-of-time testing.
Planned Use: Direct competitor; distinguish continuous operating deterioration, calibration decay, GenAI-era split, and rewrite robustness.
Verification: Primary arXiv page and paper reviewed

Title: Auditing Predictive Information in SEC 10-K Text: Evidence from a 50-Firm U.S. Large-Cap Pilot
Document / Data: SEC 10-K text for a 50-firm U.S. large-cap pilot
Method: Out-of-sample audit of predictive information in filing text
Key Finding: Provides a recent direct audit of whether 10-K text contains stable out-of-sample predictive information.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Narrows any claim of being the first reliability or predictive-audit study of 10-K text.
Planned Use: Direct competitor; treat pilot scope and exact outcomes cautiously pending full-paper review.
Verification: Primary SSRN page and PDF metadata reviewed

Authors: Chin, Michael; Liu, Yue; Moffitt, Kevin
Title: Voluntary Disclosure Through the Prominence of Risk Factors in the 10-K
Document / Data: Ordering and prominence of Item 1A risk factors
Method: Structural disclosure measures linked to future adverse outcomes
Outcome / Task: Credit downgrades, bankruptcy, and goodwill impairments
Key Finding: The order of risk factors conveys incremental information about which risks are more likely to materialize.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Shows that structure and ordering—not only wording—can predict future outcomes.
Planned Use: Add prominence/order controls so style drift is not confused with structural information.
Verification: Author-institution research brief and paper citation reviewed

Authors: Blann, James Justin; Moon, James R.; Wang, Yuxiao
Title: Risk Factor Disclosure Summaries
Document / Data: SEC-mandated Item 1A summaries and LLM-generated benchmark summaries
Method: Comparison of firm-provided summaries with LLM benchmark summaries
Outcome / Task: Information content and reporting quality of risk summaries
Key Finding: Studies whether shortened disclosure representations preserve material risk information.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Relevant to summarization, omission risk, and controlled transformation validation.
Verification: Primary SSRN page and accounting-conference listing reviewed

Authors: Jia, Ning; Li, Ningzhong; Xu, Da; Zhang, Yuwen
Title: When IR Meets GenAI
Method: Empirical analysis of GenAI use in investor-relations settings
Outcome / Task: Corporate communication practices and market information
Key Finding: Provides evidence that GenAI is entering investor-relations workflows and changing communication production.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports the GenAI-era motivation without establishing filing authorship.

Authors: Jia, Ning; Li, Ningzhong; Ma, Guang; Xu, Da
Title: Corporate Responses to Generative AI: Early Evidence from Conference Calls
Method: Empirical study of corporate discussion and response to generative AI
Outcome / Task: Firm responses, disclosure, and economic behavior
Key Finding: Documents early corporate responses to GenAI using capital-market communications.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Provides contemporaneous context for the post-2022 period but not 10-K predictive reliability.

Authors: Cho, Tony; Huang, Allen H.; Pacelli, Joseph; Rennekamp, Kristina
Title: Generative AI and Investor Processing of Financial Media
Document / Data: Financial media and GenAI-supported investor information processing
Key Finding: Examines how GenAI changes the way investors process financial information.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Adjacent to downstream use of transformed financial text, rather than issuer-side model decay.

Authors: Cao, Sean Shun; Chen, Wilbur Xinyuan; Ma, Guang; Srinivasan, Suraj
Title: Generative AI in Capital Markets: Information Production, Consumption, and Intermediation
Document / Data: Research synthesis across capital-market participants and disclosures
Method: Framework and synthesis of emerging empirical evidence
Key Finding: Frames GenAI as affecting both creation and processing of financial information.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: High-level literature boundary for claims about GenAI-era capital markets.
Verification: Primary working-paper and journal metadata reviewed

Authors: Marin, Lucas G. Uberti-Bona; Rijsbosch, Bram; Spanakis, Gerasimos; Kollnig, Konrad
Title: Are Companies Taking AI Risks Seriously? A Systematic Analysis of Companies’ AI Risk Disclosures in SEC 10-K Forms
Method: Large-scale extraction and analysis of AI-related risk disclosures
Outcome / Task: Prevalence, content, and specificity of AI-risk language
Key Finding: AI-risk mentions rose sharply, while many disclosures remained generic.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Direct observed-language neighbor and important confound: firms may mention AI because their business risks changed.
Planned Use: Exclude/control explicit AI-risk discussion and measure generic versus firm-specific AI language.

Title: ARQA: Auditable Reasoning for Financial Question Answering
Document / Data: Financial documents with reasoning and evidence
Outcome / Task: Financial question answering with traceable evidence
Key Finding: Evaluates whether model answers can be traced to explicit financial evidence and reasoning.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports auditability requirements for evidence-grounded features and explanations.

Title: FinVerBench: Benchmarking Verifiable Financial Reasoning
Document / Data: Financial facts, claims, and supporting evidence
Method: Benchmark for verification and grounded reasoning
Key Finding: Separates fluent financial responses from answers that can be verified against evidence.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Directly informs factual-preservation and claim-verification tests.

Authors: Dolphin, Robert; Dursun, Irem; Blankenship, Jeff; Adams, Griffin; Pike, Christopher
Title: Grounded Event Extraction from SEC 8-K Filings
Method: Evidence-linked extraction of material corporate events
Outcome / Task: Grounded event identification and source linkage
Key Finding: Demonstrates a pipeline for extracting structured corporate events while retaining supporting disclosure evidence.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Methodological precedent for evidence-linked narrative features.

Authors: Bettencourt, Jesse; Ding, Yuxuan; Giesecke, Kay
Title: The Stanford EDGAR Filings Dataset
Document / Data: Large structured corpus of SEC EDGAR filings
Key Finding: Provides a modern large-scale SEC filing resource and standardized processing framework.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Important engineering comparator, although our point-in-time lineage may require an independent pipeline.
Planned Use: Data-engineering comparison and possible validation source.

Authors: Long, Yicheng; Hu, Yifan; Zhao, Yilun; Cohan, Arman; Zhao, Yilun
Title: FinLFQA: A Long-Form Financial Question Answering Benchmark
Method: Long-form financial QA with document grounding
Outcome / Task: Faithful synthesis and reasoning over financial evidence
Key Finding: Benchmarks long-form financial reasoning where factual support and citation quality matter.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports evidence-linked explanation evaluation rather than style-only predictions.

Authors: Guo, Yuchen; Wu, Shijie; Yiu, Siu-Ming
Title: FinGround: A Benchmark for Grounded Financial Generation
Document / Data: Financial source documents, claims, and generated responses
Key Finding: Evaluates whether generated financial claims are supported by the supplied evidence.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Useful for rewrite preservation and evidence-linked model explanations.

Authors: Yang, Yucheng; Zhang, Yiming; Li, Zhenyu; Chen, Qian; Wang, Haoyu; Liu, Zhiyuan
Title: FinMRAGBench: Benchmarking Multi-Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Finance
Document / Data: Multiple financial documents and evidence-intensive questions
Key Finding: Shows the difficulty of retrieving and synthesizing the correct evidence across financial documents.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Supports rigorous source retrieval and evidence coverage in the robust model.

Title: How Much of a 10-K Matters? Aggregation-Dependent Value of Full-Text versus Risk-Factor Sentiment
Method: Supervised lexicon learning against return and volatility labels at sector, portfolio, and individual-firm aggregation levels
Outcome / Task: Return and realized-volatility sentiment classification and correlation with market outcomes
Key Finding: Full-filing text performs better at sector and portfolio levels, while Item 1A performs better at the individual-firm level; the result depends on aggregation and available training signal.
Overlap with Disclosure Drift: Important late-breaking comparator for full-text versus section-specific modeling and supervised 10-K language measures, but not a GenAI-era temporal reliability, calibration, operating-outcome, or rewrite study.
Planned Use: Require section-specific and aggregation-level robustness checks; avoid claiming novelty for comparing full 10-K text with Item 1A.
